Elongation (ER) and Isotropy (IR) ratios from the orientation tensor

Source: R/stats.R
compute_ei.Rd

Constructs the 3 x 3 orientation (fabric) tensor of the scar directions of one core, computes its eigenvalues \(\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \lambda_3\), and returns the elongation and isotropy ratios $$ER = 1 - \lambda_2 / \lambda_1, \quad IR = \lambda_3 / \lambda_1.$$ As for compute_spi(), each is returned raw, rarefied, and with its random interval at the core's scar count.

Usage

compute_ei(
  dx,
  dy,
  dz,
  raw = TRUE,
  rarefied = TRUE,
  random_interval = TRUE,
  m = 3,
  max_comb = 2000,
  seed = 2226
)

Arguments

dx, dy, dz

Numeric vectors of equal length: the X, Y and Z components of the scar direction vectors of one core, for example End_X - Start_X etc., or the d_x, d_y, d_z columns returned by align_scar_batch(). The vectors are normalised to unit length inside the function; rows of zero length or with missing values are left out.

raw

Logical. Return the raw ratios (ER_raw, IR_raw) and the eigenvalues? Default TRUE.

rarefied

Logical. Return the rarefied ratios (ER_rarefied, IR_rarefied)? Default TRUE.

random_interval

Logical. Return the random intervals (ER_lower, ER_upper, IR_lower, IR_upper) and the position of the raw ratios relative to them (ER_vs_random, IR_vs_random)? Default TRUE.

m

Number of scars per combination for the rarefied value. Default 3.

max_comb

Largest number of combinations averaged. Above it, max_comb distinct combinations are drawn at random (a Monte Carlo approximation of the mean over all combinations). Default 2000.

seed

Seed for that random draw; the caller's random stream is restored afterwards. NULL draws from the current stream. Default 2226.

Value

A one-row tibble with n_scar, then for ER and for IR the columns selected by raw, rarefied and random_interval (*_raw, *_rarefied, *_lower, *_upper, *_vs_random), and, with raw = TRUE, the eigenvalues lambda1, lambda2, lambda3 of the orientation tensor of all scars. All values are NA for cores with fewer than three scars.

Details

ER measures how far the scars are aligned along one axis, whether they run the same way or opposite ways; IR measures how far the scar directions spread into three dimensions (low IR: directions concentrated in a plane or along an axis). ER above the upper bound and IR below the lower bound of the random interval indicate directions more concentrated than random.

Raw ER and IR shift with the scar count; compare cores and groups with the rarefied values (see compute_spi()). Negative eigenvalues caused by numerical error are clamped to zero, and both ratios are NA when \(\lambda_1 \approx 0\).

Changes in 0.2.0. The columns E and I are renamed ER_raw and IR_raw; the input vectors are normalised inside the function.

References

Lin, S. C., Clarkson, C., Julianto, I. M. A., Ferdianto, A., Jatmiko, & Sutikna, T. (2024). A new method for quantifying flake scar organisation on cores using orientation statistics. Journal of Archaeological Science, 167, 105998.

McPherron, S. P. (2018). Additional statistical and graphical methods for analyzing site formation processes using artifact orientations. PLOS ONE, 13(1), e0190195.

See also

compute_spi(), spi_ei_batch(), random_interval()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- matrix(rnorm(45), 15, 3)
compute_ei(d[, 1], d[, 2], d[, 3])
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   n_scar ER_raw ER_rarefied ER_lower ER_upper ER_vs_random IR_raw IR_rarefied
#>    <int>  <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1     15  0.507       0.622   0.0668    0.576 within        0.221      0.0582
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: IR_lower <dbl>, IR_upper <dbl>, IR_vs_random <chr>,
#> #   lambda1 <dbl>, lambda2 <dbl>, lambda3 <dbl>
